subject: Business Models
title: Webvan: Too Early, Too Big
description: One-minute skill: Webvan: Too Early, Too Big.

hook.text: Webvan raised $800 million to deliver groceries online in 1999. It burned through all of it in 18 months.

buildup.text: Webvan built massive automated warehouses in 10 cities before proving demand in even one city.

discovery.text: The model required enormous capital: warehouses, delivery trucks, cold chains—all before a single profitable order.

twist.text: Twenty years later, Instacart proved the model works—using existing stores and gig drivers. No warehouses needed.

climax.text: Webvan's idea was right but its model was wrong. Capital-light delivery beat capital-heavy warehouse-first.

punchline.text: $800M, 18 months, bankrupt. Right idea, wrong decade, wrong model.

quiz.question: What was Webvan's key strategic mistake?
options: Building massive infrastructure before proving demand

details.summary: Webvan tried to build an automated grocery delivery empire in 1999, investing over 1 billion dollars in massive robotic warehouses before proving customer demand. The infrastructure was built for scale that never came, and Webvan collapsed in 2001 as one of the dot-com era's biggest failures.
details.whyItMatters: Webvan proves that building infrastructure before demand is confirmed is catastrophically expensive. Its model was eventually proven viable by Instacart and Amazon Fresh.
takeaways: One billion dollars invested in automated warehouses before demand was proven
Infrastructure scaled for volume that never materialized before cash ran out
Instacart later proved the model by starting asset-light and scaling gradually

faq.question: What was Webvan's fundamental strategic mistake?
faq.answer: Building a billion dollars of infrastructure before proving consistent customer demand. Each automated warehouse needed massive order volume to break even. By expanding to 10 markets simultaneously instead of perfecting one, Webvan multiplied its burn rate tenfold.

faq.question: How did later grocery delivery companies avoid Webvan's mistakes?
faq.answer: Instacart used existing grocery stores and contract shoppers instead of building warehouses. It started in one city and expanded only after proving unit economics. Amazon Fresh leveraged existing Prime subscriber base and fulfillment infrastructure. Both proved demand before investing.
